author: JEFF SMITH
title: Jury finds California man guilty of murder and attempted murder of Polson officer - NewsBreak
text:
By JEFF SMITH ,
5 hours ago
It took a Lake County jury two and a half hours to find a California man guilty of murder and attempted murder. Cameron Francis, 50, was charged with deliberate homicide and attempted deliberate homicide for the shooting death of his girlfriend and for firing multiple rounds at a Polson police officer. According to charging documents, the charges stem from an incident late on the night of Feb. 14, 2025. Francis allegedly fired 20 rounds from an assault rifle at a Polson police officer's patrol car before he fled and fired seven more rounds at him. The rounds showered the officer with broken glass. Police apprehended Francis within an hour in the Elmo area, where he surrendered. The following Sunday, a request for a welfare check on Francis’s girlfriend was called in, leading police to her Polson residence and her dead body. Lake County Attorney James Lapotka explained in charging documents that she died from a single gunshot to the face. Shell casings at both scenes matched an assault rifle found in the Honda Accord that Francis was driving. The trial began with jury selection on Oct. 23 and opening arguments on Oct. 26.
